text:
Ana (Docs): FYI I opened a PR to expand the model card for redwood/mistral-7b and to add a short migration checklist for the quantized variant. Things I put in the draft: supported contexts, a tiny benchmark summary, SDK examples, and a compatibility note. Draft PR: https://git.internal/redwood/docs/pull/468

docs-bot: PR created: #468 docs/model-catalog/mistral-7b: add migration checklist + compatibility notes (Ana (Docs))

Sam (ML): Nice start. Quick bench numbers from our lab run (A100-80GB, kv cache warm, single stream, 1 request concurrent):
```
sequence=512 -> 6.9 ms/token (median), ~1450 tok/s
sequence=2048 -> 10.5 ms/token (median), ~980 tok/s
memory_peak(512) ~9.2GB, (2048) ~17.6GB
```
I'll upload the CSV to the PR comments and tag it `bench-mistral-2026-02` so other teams can reproduce. Note: quant variant shows ~10% higher latency when kernel fallback happens.

Devon (Runtime): One thing to call out under "Compatibility / Known issues": quant builds currently trigger a float-kernel fallback for some attention patterns on driver combos older than CUDA 11.8. Recommend wording like: "Quant variants may execute float kernels for a subset of layers on older CUDA + driver combinations, increasing latency and memory use. For low-latency workloads (continuous_batching enabled) prefer the full-precision build until runtime issue #789 is resolved." Also add the runtime fallback log snippet users will see: 
```
[runtime] WARN fallback: quant_kernels_unavailable -> executing float path for layer 12
```
And mention recommended minimum: CUDA >=11.8, driver >=528.x.

Zack (SDK): Adding two short SDK snippets to the PR — Python (pinned version) and TS. Use `model_version` to pin stable behavior. Python sample: 
```python
from redwood import Client
c = Client()
r = c.generate(model="redwood/mistral-7b", model_version="2026-02-15", prompt="Explain mutexes in simple terms", max_tokens=120)
print(r.output_text)
```
TS sample: 
```ts
import { Redwood } from '@redwood/inference'
const client = new Redwood()
const resp = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood/mistral-7b', model_version: '2026-02-15', prompt: 'Explain mutexes in simple terms', max_tokens: 120 })
console.log(resp.output_text)
```
I'll push a tiny edit to the PR with those. Also note: structured responses are now returned under `output_text` for backwards-compatibility in the Python SDK.

Lina (CS): Heads up — add a one-line "what to tell customers" in the doc so support can copy-paste. Something like: "If you see higher latency after switching to quant: run the eval suite `mistral-compat-2026q1`, verify your CUDA/driver version, and temporarily pin to the non-quant model or enable fallback routing." Also ask Ana to drop a note in #release-notes when merged.

Ana (Docs): Will add the one-liner and a short migration checklist: 1) run `mistral-compat-2026q1` eval, 2) pin `model_version`, 3) test latency on target infra at 512/2048 seq, 4) if OOMs or stalls occur enable fallback route or use non-quant. I'll include the `WARN fallback` log example Devon provided.

Sam (ML): Extra request: please include the bench methodology: batch size (1), concurrency (1), warm-up passes (20), tool: `rw-bench v0.7`. That helps reproduce.

Zack (SDK): One more tiny note — the README example that links to this card currently references the old param `version` — I'll update it to `model_version` in a separate tiny PR and link it from this model card.

Ana (Docs): Great. I'll keep PR as draft until Sam's CSV and Zack's TS snippet are in. TODOs in PR body: attach bench CSV (Sam), add TS snippet (Zack), add CUDA driver minimum (Devon), add customer-facing blurb (Lina). Merge when all approved. :white_check_mark:
